title: Take out the trash: cinch and remove a loaded drawstring liner
instruction: Pull both drawstrings to close the full bag, lift it out of the bin by the drawstrings, and set it down upright on the table beside the bin without spilling any contents.
context: Taking out a small kitchen or bathroom bin at home: pull the liner's two drawstring loops so the mouth closes, lift the loaded bag out by the strings and put it down without spilling. Uses an unmodified commercial drawstring liner and its normal closure; no knot, lock, clip or added handle.
setup: simplehuman Code A drawstring liner (4.5 L, about 29 x 40 cm flat, white) fitted in an IKEA NYPON 15 cm pot (art. 603.956.16; 17.1 cm outside / 15.9 cm inside diameter, 15.2 cm tall, polypropylene, taped to the mat) centred at (0.22, 0) m, surplus folded down over the rim so the hem hangs about 2 cm above the mat. The two exposed drawstring loops are hooked out of their cut-outs and lie on the mat pointing outward, far ends at y = +/-0.16 m. Three clean 70 x 100 x 45 mm, 50 g mock-waste blocks inside, long side along y: two standing side by side on a 45 x 100 mm face (x = 0.1965/0.2435, y = 0), one lying flat on top (x = 0.22). Two YAM arms at (0, +/-0.305, 0.750), table top z = 0.7475, 800 x 1000 x 2.5 mm mat. Full layout, sources and a hand preflight of liner and closure in PHYSICAL_PROTOCOL.md.
scoring: Highest level met; failures latch. 0: opening never <= 80 mm, any block leaves the bag, bag destroyed, or invalid simulation. 0.25: cinched (opening <= 80 mm, smaller than a block's 83 mm smallest-face diagonal; three blocks inside). 0.5: then carried: opening <= 80 mm when the whole bag first clears the rim by 20 mm (contents included). 0.75: at the end resting upright on the table (mouth >= 150 mm above it, bottom within 25 mm), >= 20 mm clear of the pot and table edges, opening <= 80 mm. 1.0: that state, opening included, for the final 2 s with both grippers >= 60 mm from film and loops and bag bounds moving <= 10 mm. Measured with ruler/video and a block count; see PHYSICAL_PROTOCOL.md.
run_limit: 4,000 control steps at 20 Hz (200 simulated seconds); requested CLI seed 0, installed adapter environment seed 42, no object jitter.
reset_notes: Fresh unmodified liner each trial: bottom flat in the pot, surplus folded over the rim, cut-outs facing the arms, each loop hooked out and laid flat on the mat at its marked spot without gathering the mouth. Three blocks in place, arms at ready, tabletop beside the pot clear.
fidelity: PhysX deformable film folded over the rim, rigid blocks, standard robot and gripper, contact grasps, no scripted poses. Each loop's pinch point is a 2 g rigid body (no stable sim string); the real trial uses the unmodified loop with no handle, so the sim grasp is easier. String: force-only routed spring, no lock, 0.7 N cap. Opening may widen to about 100 mm while swinging in transit; containment is checked every step (8 mm centres, 20 mm corners). 0.10 mm film; straight pot. No physical trial.
scores: Scripted demo, official Arena release/0.3.1: 1.0 (FB_ol1, replay 1.0); repeat 0.5 (80.15 mm). 1.0 in 3 of 6 runs across two environments; failure: mouth springs open to about 80 mm at release. Dream-1: errored at step 1,427 (out-of-range gripper reply rejected); not scored; session not lost.
